articles.title: Juan Carlos Rivero se pronuncia sobre Netflix y el Mundial 2030: "Es un negociazo, pero..."
articles.standfirst: El narrador de los partidos en TVE concedió una entrevista a 'Otra Ronda' en Radio MARCA aprovechando el 70 cumpleaños de la televisión pública
articles.summary: El narrador de los partidos en TVE concedió una entrevista a 'Otra Ronda' en Radio MARCA aprovechando el 70 cumpleaños de la televisión pública
articles.body: Juan Carlos Rivero lleva más de cuatro décadas contando el deporte y ha aprendido que, en televisión, no siempre se puede controlar lo que sucede delante de una cámara ni lo que ocurre después en las redes sociales. El periodista de Televisión Española fue el protagonista de una nueva entrega de 'Otra Ronda', el programa de Radio MARCA presentado por Carlos Vicente 'Chitu', en una entrevista marcada por los 70 años de TVE. Rivero no esconde la emoción que le produce recordar aquella final. «Es que este es un momento histórico. Es una felicidad y una fortuna estar en el momento adecuado, en el lugar adecuado», explica sobre la oportunidad de narrar un partido de semejante dimensión. El periodista también tuvo un recuerdo para los grandes narradores que le precedieron en TVE y que no pudieron vivir una experiencia similar con la selección española. «Me acordé de todos aquellos grandes narradores que Televisión Española ha tenido y que no habían tenido la fortuna de poder narrar algo así», confiesa aclarando el ciclo triunfal de España que fue desde 2008 a 2012. Rivero se siente especialmente agradecido por haber podido contar un triunfo de España en una televisión pública y en abierto, ante millones de espectadores. «Tener la oportunidad de estarlo contando en la televisión que lo está dando en abierto a millones de personas es una satisfacción muy grande», asegura. «Ya he visto que conmigo se ha hecho personaje», admite. Lejos de enfrentarse a esa imagen pública, decidió asumirla: «He seguido el juego. En vez de intentar surfear la ola en contra, me he subido a la ola y voy a favor; es decir, que si hay que reírse, yo me río el primero». Rivero defiende que narrar un partido de fútbol en directo es una tarea compleja en la que resulta prácticamente imposible no equivocarse. «Es imposible no cometer un error, no equivocarse durante dos horas en un juego donde hay 22 más otros 10 que pueden entrar», argumenta, aludiendo al movimiento constante de los futbolistas, los contactos y la dificultad de identificar cada acción en décimas de segundo. El periodista no niega sus limitaciones, pero tampoco permite que estas condicionen su manera de trabajar. «Que conmigo se hayan viralizado más los errores, bueno, pues nada, sigamos el juego», resume. Y añade una idea que explica su actitud: «No pretendo ser ni el mejor ni perfecto». Para el periodista, aquel torneo supuso algo más que un éxito deportivo. Le permitió desprenderse de la imagen distante que algunos aficionados tenían de él y mostrar una personalidad más espontánea. «Empecé a ser más yo que nunca, a comportarme como yo era, sin filtros», explica. Rivero considera que la televisión puede imponer una formalidad excesiva y que la naturalidad ayuda a conectar con la audiencia. «A medida que iba siendo yo y trataba de ser sin artificios, veía que la gente se lo tomaba mejor», recuerda. Ese cambio de percepción también se refleja en su relación con las críticas. El periodista asegura que se toma con humor incluso los comentarios negativos que le llegan a través de su entorno familiar. «Me gusta reírme mucho de las cosas y de mí mismo el primero», afirma. Y esa es, probablemente, una de las claves de su nueva conexión con el público: entender que detrás de la voz que narra los grandes partidos también hay una persona capaz de equivocarse, reírse de sí misma y seguir adelante. La respuesta del periodista a la noticia de la compra de Derechos por parte de Netflix en 2030 fue una reivindicación del valor de los grandes acontecimientos deportivos en abierto. «Eso te demuestra el mérito inmenso que tiene ofrecer grandes eventos deportivos en abierto», sostiene. Rivero entiende que las plataformas de pago entren en el negocio y que las organizaciones deportivas busquen maximizar sus ingresos. Sin embargo, cree que el dinero no es el único factor que debe tenerse en cuenta a la hora de valorar los derechos audiovisuales. «Al final, entre el dinero y la difusión, prevalece o está prevaleciendo a última hora la difusión», señala, poniendo como ejemplo la enorme capacidad de convocatoria de los Juegos Olímpicos y de los grandes torneos futbolísticos. «No me parece ni bien ni mal que la FIFA le venda el Mundial a Netflix. Entiendo que es un negocio tremendo, pero al final aparecerá alguna cadena en abierto que es quien dará los mejores partidos y de quien se hablará a última hora», pronostica. Rivero recordó sus primeros pasos en el periodismo deportivo, cuando acudía a Vallecas para cubrir partidos y cobraba seis euros por intervención, y su llegada a 'Estudio Estadio', el programa con el que ha mantenido una relación prácticamente permanente a lo largo de los años. Ahora, con más de cuatro décadas de trayectoria a sus espaldas, el periodista asegura que no siente el paso del tiempo como una carga. «Estoy súper contento de todo este tiempo, sobre todo de lo bien que me lo he pasado», explica.

articles.title: Oregon HSFB Coach Fired After Onside Kicks in 63-0 Win, Game Called at Halftime
articles.summary: An Oregon high school football coach was fired after his team ran up the score in the first half of a game on Friday, according to Mark Puleo of The Athletic.
articles.body:
An Oregon high school football coach was fired after his team ran up the score in the first half of a game on Friday, according to Mark Puleo of The Athletic.

Per Puleo, Marist Catholic High parted ways with head coach Zach Loboy following a 63-0 victory over Cottage Grove High that was called at halftime. Loboy's team attempted two onside kicks before the first half came to a close, while Cottage Grove High only had 16 players available.

Marist Catholic principal Bob Fraley released a statement in an email to football parents and guardians regarding Loboy's dismissal.

"I am writing to inform you that Marist has made the decision to remove Zach Loboy from his position as Head Varsity Football Coach, effective immediately," Fraley wrote in the email, per KVAL . "Following Friday's game against Cottage Grove, we determined that a change in leadership was necessary to reflect our school's mission and values."

Marist Catholic athletic director Rick Gardner also discussed the coaching decision.

"What happened there is really not reflective of the school's mission and how we want to treat our opponents," Gardner told Jarrid Denney of the Eugene Register-Guard . "Our athletic program tries to adhere to the mission and the values of Marist Catholic High School. In this particular case, we definitely fell short."

Marist Catholic previously won the Oregon Class 4A state championship in 2024 and owns a 3-3 record this year.

articles.title: El informe de La Masia que desaconsejaba el fichaje de Messi en el 2000: "Creo que no se debe fichar"
articles.standfirst: Florent Torchut, periodista de France Football, desvela los escritos de tres informadores
articles.summary: Florent Torchut, periodista de France Football, desvela los escritos de tres informadores
articles.body: Florent Torchut, periodista de France Football, ha desvelado en su cuenta de X tres informes realizados por formadores de La Masia en el año 2000 sobre Leo Messi. Dos de ellos eran favorables a su fichaje, mientras que otro lo desaconsejaba. "Considero que es un jugador de una calidad técnica indiscutible, pero su limitación física (142 cm) es demasiada para poder competir ahora mismo en su categoría. Y el año que viene todavía más, porque aunque crezca, con 150 cm y la diferencia de complexión física que presenta será muy complicado jugar en cadete preferente. Creo que no se debe fichar. Como mucho, seguir su evolución y volver a probarlo dentro de un par de años", apuntaba uno de los informadores, el que no aconsejaba ficharle. Los otros dos informes, sin embargo, sí eran favorables a su fichaje. "Salvando las distancias, es un Maradona (pequeño de edad). Yo le ficharía, tiene que ir a mucho más. Ya veremos su evolución", apuntaba uno de ellos. "Por su edad, es un jugador técnicamente muy completo. Destaca sobre sus compañeros: tiene visión de jugada, es ágil, es vivo, listo, un dribling muy bueno, pase bueno, es un jugador muy completo y sobresale de todos sus compañeros. Chuta bien y fuerte, en el uno contra uno es muy bueno, pero es bajito. Le falta físico, no va por alto (estatura). Los rivales la mayoría son superiores en físico. Gran jugador", señalaba el otro. El Barça hizo caso a los dos informes favorables y terminó fichando a Leo Messi poco después, con 13 años. El resto es historia.

articles.title: Europa es muy cruel
articles.standfirst: Un gol de Kolo Muani en el 93' firma una nueva derrota celeste en Europa League
articles.summary: Un gol de Kolo Muani en el 93' firma una nueva derrota celeste en Europa League
articles.body: El Celta volvió a vivir una noche nefasta en Europa. La depresión se prolongó con un gol de Kolo Muani en el minuto 93 que confirmaba la remontada de la Juve en Balaídos. La segunda derrota en esta Europa League de los de Giráldez, que no levantan cabeza. Ni siquiera el parón ha conseguido revertir una dinámica que empieza a ser preocupante. El drama no cesa. A veces, uno pierde su identidad de manera deliberada. En otras, ocurre porque no hay más remedio. Porque las circunstancias te llevan a ello. Llámenle circunstancias o Juventus de Turín. El equipo italiano hizo honor a su condición de histórico en Europa y se presentó en Balaídos señalando a su escudo. Dominaron los de Spalletti. Sometieron, por momentos, a un Celta acostumbrado a ser protagonista con balón. No iba a ser el caso en esta noche de Europa League. Es cierto, eso sí, que el equipo italiano sobó la pelota, insinuó en el último tercio pero apenas concretó nada -hasta el tramo final-. Radu solo tuvo que sacar un par de buenas manos en todo el partido. No es, salta a la vista, la Juve temible de las grandes noches de Champions. Pero aun con eso le bastó para ser mejor, merecer la victoria y conseguirla sobre la bocina. En medio de ese orden defensivo que se instaló durante casi todo el partido, de ese control obligado en campo propio, el Celta encontró su momento. La jugada, por cierto, fue de máximo nivel. Una transición que llevó el balón de lado a lado y que terminó en el área en los pies de Swedberg, con la suficiente sangre fría para ceder a Hugo Álvarez y que este marcase a placer. El guión no se alteró, más bien se acentuó tras el golpe celeste. Con Conceiçao atacando la profundidad y Woltemade haciendo de pivote de fútbol sala. Ambos generando más de un dolor de cabeza a la zaga celeste. Sin embargo, la sensación era que los de Spalletti disparaban con balas de fogueo. Hacían algo de ruido, pero no generaban daño alguno. Tuvo que surgir un error individual. Grosero, inexplicable para alguien de la experiencia de Marcos Alonso. El defensa quiso ceder o controlar con el pecho, no se sabe bien cuál de ambas, y el balón se convirtió en un caramelo para que Woltemade lo mandase a la jaula sin envoltorio. El Celta, más con corazón y empuje que juego, encontró alguna que otra transición que no supo finalizar con templanza. La precipitación le alejó del acierto, y eso terminó por condenarlo. Ni siquiera la entrada de Aspas, para dotar al partido de un toque emocional, sirvió para encontrar el camino de la gloria. Más bien todo lo contrario. Porque los cambios de Spalletti venían con premio. En el último suspiro, en el último balón colgado a la desesperada, el recién incorporado Kolo Muani cabeceó casi debajo de la portería. Con Marcos Alonso de nuevo en la foto, con Radu a la expectativa. Y los puntos volaron otra vez de Balaídos. Una fea costumbre esta temporada. Una terrible rutina que empieza a poner en tela de juicio un proyecto que sufre sus primeros temblores en el mes de octubre. Mala señal.

articles.title: Álvaro Rodríguez se estrena con el Bournemouth en la victoria europea
articles.standfirst: El delantero nacido en España firmó su primer tanto con los 'Cherries' en el 3-0 de los ingleses al Sturn Graz
articles.summary: El delantero nacido en España firmó su primer tanto con los 'Cherries' en el 3-0 de los ingleses al Sturn Graz
articles.body: El encuentro entre los Olympique de Marsella y Olympiacos comenzó muy parejo, con ambos equipos resistiendo para no ceder ante el rival. Sin embargo, los griegos fueron los primeros en golpear. En un córner, Hezze se adelantó en el primer palo y con un cabezazo deshizo el empate. Antes del descanso la diferencia podía haber sido mayor, pero el gol de Yaremchuk no subió al marcador por fuera de juego. El conjunto de Imanol Alguacil estaba completando la misión, ganando el partido y manteniendo a raya a los franceses. Stefan Ortega fue uno de los nombres destacados de la noche, evitando que el Marsella consiguiese igualar. Los griegos supieron sufrir y resistir los ataques galos y con el tanto del argentino, el Olympiacos suma su segunda victoria en esta fase de liga de la Conference y suma más argumentos a su candidatura por el título. El Sturn Graz estaba logrando resistir al Bournemouth. Sin embargo, al borde del descanso cedió la defensa austriaca con un cabezazo de Evanilson a una distancia considerable. Los ingleses tuvieron que insistir para volver a penetrar la red de su rival. Pero tras un córner, Rayan iba a aprovechar el rechace del portero para batir con un disparo raso. En el descuento, Álvaro Rodríguez iba a poner la guinda a la noche marcando su primer gol con el club en seis partidos, transformando la pena máxima. El Benfica quería seguir con el buen pie en Europa. Y no tardó mucho en adelantarse el conjunto portugués, ya que Jhon Durán consiguió anotar la pena máxima a los cinco minutos. Menos de 20 minutos después, Prestianni mandó un gran centro al área, que Bah de primeras remató de volea y duplicó la distancia. A falta de 10 para el descanso, Durán volvió a marcar tras recibir de Prestianni, deshacerse de su par y definir con la izquierda. Pero los escoceses no fueron a Portugal a pasearse. Martin O'Neill realizó cuatro cambios en apenas 20 minutos. Camilo Durán se adelantó al portero del Benfica y con un cabezazo a pase de Haissem Hassan, recortó distancias. Querían más y Camilo Durán tuvo otra ocasión para el segundo, pero su potente disparo se estrelló contra el palo. El Benfica tenía algo que decir y Schjelderup replicó con un remate violento que también se fue contra la madera. Cerca de acabar, Pavlidis acabó con cualquier esperanza de remontada y tras engañar con su definición al portero rival, puso el cuarto y definitivo tanto del conjunto luso. El Brighton quería encadenar su quinta victoria consecutiva. Sin embargo, el Zalgiris estaba consiguiendo resistir. Pero al borde del descanso, una gran jugada de Osman, que parecía que se había salido del campo, puso un pase al corazón del área y Rutter con una buena definición puso el primero de los ingleses. Aunque antes de irse a los vestuarios, Hinshelwood aumentaría la ventaja tras cruzar un el balón tras el pase de Rutter. Tras reanudarse el juego, 'las gaviotas' querían seguir imponiendo su juego y certificar la victoria. Rutter volvió a encargarse, empujando el balón al fondo de la red tras el pase de Osman. Los ingleses no cesaban en seguir aumentando la cuenta, y O'Reilly con un buen remate de cabeza puso el cuarto a pase de Ibrahim apenas llevaba segundos en el campo y así el Brighton certificó su quinta victoria consecutiva entre todas las competiciones.

articles.title: Lyon down Palace in Europa League, Sunderland leave it late
articles.summary: French club Lyon held off Crystal Palace 3-2 in the Europa League on Thursday, while Sunderland made a late comeback to break the hearts of Portuguese second...
articles.body:
French club Lyon held off Crystal Palace 3-2 in the Europa League on Thursday, while Sunderland made a late comeback to break the hearts of Portuguese second-division side Torreense.

Bayer Leverkusen, Juventus, Benfica and Bournemouth all also won to maintain their perfect starts to the league phase.

It was a painful return to his old home for Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage as the UEFA Conference League champions fell to their fourth defeat of the season in all competitions.

"It's a very disappointing return because we lost. I can't take satisfaction from coming back home or seeing familiar faces when the result isn't there," Sage told UEFA.com.

"The scoreline may have been close, but there was a big difference in the way the two teams played. We were nowhere near our usual standards in the first half."

Lyon took the lead inside the opening 10 minutes through Corentin Tolisso and Ernest Nuamah then doubled Lyon's advantage two minutes into first-half injury time.

Yeremy Pino halved the deficit for Palace early in the second period, but a close-range flick by Pavel Sulc restored Lyon's two-goal buffer.

Daichi Kamada smashed home a second for Palace with nine minutes remaining but the hosts held out to make it two wins from two to start the league phase.

Bayer Leverkusen followed up their opening 2-0 win with a 4-0 success at Polish side Lech Poznan.

AC Milan cruised to a 4-0 victory at Red Bull Salzburg, courtesy of a hat-trick scored by Italian teenager Alphadjo Cisse.

Club-record signing Goncalo Ramos made it four on 72 minutes before a red card for Filippo Terracciano took some of the sheen off the win for Ruben Amorim's men.

In the Estadio Municipal de Leiria, Portuguese Cup winners Torreense looked set to hold their Premier League opponents to a draw until Noah Sadiki's 93rd-minute strike made it 2-1 for the visitors.

The 15th-placed side in Portugal's second tier stunned Sunderland in the 37th minute as centre-half Volnei Feltes cut past a flimsy challenge and unleashed a piledriver 30 yards from goal, which left Robin Roefs rooted to the spot.

Black Cats boss Regis Le Bris sent on first-team regulars Granit Xhaka and Enzo Le Fee just shy of the hour and the move paid dividends as Jules Ahoka struck shortly afterwards to level the scores.

After a lengthy VAR check decided against awarding Sunderland a late penalty, Torreense must have thought they had done enough to earn a famous point until Sadiki popped up at the death to thrash in the winner.

"Conceding a goal in the last minute is a blow to the chest," Torreense coach Carlos Simoes said. "The players are in the dressing room, devastated."

Fellow Premier League outfit Bournemouth enjoyed a fine home debut in Europe as they eased to a 3-0 win over Sturm Graz, courtesy of goals by Evanilson, Rayan and Alvaro Rodriguez.

Juventus fought from behind to emerge 2-1 victors at Celta Vigo after Newcastle loanee Nick Woltemade made it two from two in Europe to cancel out Hugo Alvarez's opener for the hosts, and Randal Kolo Muani scored an injury-time winner.

Martin O'Neill's Celtic continued their difficult start to the season as they sank to a fourth defeat in their last five outings, outclassed 4-1 at Benfica.

articles.title: Casey Woods pushes for more Group of Six representation in expanded CFP
articles.summary: Missouri State's Casey Woods warns CFP expansion could water down the tournament. The CFP is reportedly expanding to 24 teams in 2027.
articles.body:
SPRINGFIELD — The college football playoff landscape is changing once again.

The College Football Playoff is expected to set to expand to 24 teams starting in 2027, according to a report from ESPN. The current format pits the best 12 teams against each other, featuring one Group of Six team.

Missouri State head coach Casey Woods was asked about the format and how the Group of Six fits into the fold during his weekly press availability on Thursday, Oct. 15.

Woods shared that he's interested to see what happens because 'you can water it down,' suggesting teams with many losses shouldn't appear in the tournament.

"The reason you go to 24 is to access all of college football," Woods said. "You don't go to 24 to have a 12-team SEC playoff. We have to continue to push to give the G6 teams, the best ones that we've got, the opportunity to jump in there."

Missouri State football hosts Kennesaw State in Conference USA clash

Playoff expansion will obviously bring more dollars and exposure through new television deals. Woods emphasized that this expansion can't come down solely to TV executives.

"It can't simply be about television money even though I understand that's the driver," Woods said. "If we want to keep the health and the integrity of the game from a popularity standpoint, you open that up to having extended opportunities to people that have a five-loss Power-Four team just because they played a hard schedule."

Cincinnati (2021), Boise State (2024), Tulane (2025) and James Madison (2025) have all featured in the College Football Playoff as a Group of Six team. Group of Six teams are winless in their appearances in the postseason tournament.

articles.title: Brighton thrash Kauno Zalgiris in Conference League
articles.summary: Georginio Rutter scores twice as in-form Brighton begin the league phase of their Conference League campaign with a dominant home win over Lithuanian side Ka...
articles.body:
Brighton & Hove Albion 4 - 0 Kauno Žalgiris FT

Georginio Rutter scored twice as in-form Brighton began the league phase of their Conference League campaign with a dominant home victory over Lithuanian side Kauno Zalgiris.

Brighton, third in the Premier League, took 41 minutes to break down their limited opponents, who offered virtually nothing as an attacking threat.

Rutter converted from Ibrahim Osman's pullback, with the goal originally ruled out as the officials thought the ball had gone out of play only for the decision to be overruled by the video assistant referee.

It then became a question of how many Brighton would score.

Their second came just before the interval with Rutter setting up Jack Hinshelwood and the midfielder converted with a first-time effort on his return to the side after nearly two months out with an ankle injury.

The second half continued in the same one-way fashion with Hinshelwood having a header pushed over before Rutter got his second and Brighton's third, again finishing from an Osman assist.

Matt O'Riley had hit the post but seconds later made it 4-0 with a header following a cross from 18-year-old Egyptian midfielder Younes Ibrahim, making his Brighton debut.

Three of the five winners of this third-tier European trophy have come from England - West Ham in 2023, Chelsea in 2025 and Crystal Palace in 2026 - with Brighton favourites to win the competition this season.

The Seagulls had to advance through a two-legged play-off tie against Norwegian side Tromso in August, with Brighton winning 4-0 in the second leg after a goalless draw away from home.

Brighton's fans have now seen the team score eight goals in two home European ties in 2026-27, with the club also the top scorers in the Premier League with 18 goals in six domestic league matches.

They entertain rivals Crystal Palace on Sunday before returning to the Conference League next Thursday with a trip to the Czech Republic to face Jablonec.

An easy night for Hurzeler's entertaining Brighton

For Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler, it was the perfect evening.

The Lithuanian visitors showed their intent early on by defending deep, camped on the edge of their penalty area in a low block, looking to frustrate the hosts.

Lewis Dunk had scored a stunning 35-yard strike in the 5-0 league win against Coventry, later named as the Premier League goal of the month for September, and the Brighton skipper was unlucky to see a long-range attempt just go over.

But the breakthrough always looked like it would come soon. Hinshelwood had a header tipped over, before Rutter got his first goal of the season to end Zalgiris' resistance.

From then on it was easy for a Brighton side that ended up with nearly 80% of possession.

Hinshelwood, Rutter again and O'Riley added further goals, with the latter denied another by a fine save from away goalkeeper Tomas Svedkauskas.

For Brighton it continues a superb season in only their second ever continental campaign.

Domestically, they have already beaten Aston Villa 4-0 and embarrassed reigning champions Arsenal 3-0 in the Premier League, and came back from 2-0 down to win 3-2 at Old Trafford and knock Manchester United out of the Carabao Cup.

Hurzeler's side have now scored 29 goals in 10 matches in all competitions and they will fancy their chances of a lengthy run in the Conference League.

articles.title: Would Texas have made CFP last year if it was expanded to 24 teams?
articles.summary: With rumors swirling the College Football Playoff will expand to 24 teams, its interesting to look back at 2025 to see if Texas would have made it.
articles.body:
It appears the College Football Playoff will be doubling next year . The current 12-team format is in its third season after expanding from the four-team CFP in 2024. The playoff system was first adopted in 2014. Now the CFP will reportedly include 24 teams in 2027. The ramifications, both good and bad, reach far and wide.

As of right now, the Longhorns are in a good position to make this year's college football playoff. But the margin for error is slim after Texas' 2nd half collapse to rival Oklahoma in the Red River Shootout. Texas would most likely enter as the No. 7 seed.

Last season, Texas missed the CFP by two spots in the final ranking . The Longhorns had three losses, to Ohio State, Florida and Georgia. Ohio State was a non-conference game. UT's exclusion from the CFP caused a lot of discussions at all levels of college football to look at non-conference scheduling. If Texas had played weaker teams, there's a good chance they would have made the bracket.

The 2025 Longhorns would have certainly benefitted from the expanded field. Texas would have made the CFP easily and would have probably been the No. 13 seed. A projection by On3 shows Texas would have most-likely played Tulane in the first round, with the winner advancing to take on Texas Tech in Lubbock.

The new format gives eight teams a bye in the first round. It would have been interesting if Texas had played the Red Raiders, considering Texas coach Steve Sarkisian used Tech to make his point that the CFP committee should look more closely at strength of schedule.

articles.title: Félix Tainta, representante de Nico Williams: "Tenía idea de poder salir, en el Athletic sabes que no vas a ganar una Champions..."
articles.standfirst: El agente de los Williams explicó en el Podcast 'Los Fulanos' cómo fue la negociación con el Barcelona en el verano de 2025
articles.summary: El agente de los Williams explicó en el Podcast 'Los Fulanos' cómo fue la negociación con el Barcelona en el verano de 2025
articles.body: Félix Tainta, representante de Nico e Iñaki Williams, contó en el Podcast 'Los Fulanos' cómo fue la negociación con el Barcelona por Nico Williams y la posterior renovación con el Athletic. Tainta reconoce que su representado tenía intención de salir, pero que el Barcelona no le ofrecía garantías de poder ser inscrito y todo se rompió a partir de ahí. También apunta que el Athletic supo de la negociación en todo momento. Negociación con el Barcelona: "Todos sabemos del interés del Barça en el verano del 24, después de la Eurocopa. Barça, Arsenal, Bayern, Liverpool, PSG... os podría decir todos. A Nico lo han querido todos, y tener un futbolista que diga que no a todos estos clubes no es fácil. A partir de ahí, se habla con el Barça, el Athletic lo sabía porque yo informé en todo momento de cómo estaba la situación, a pesar de que el Athletic y el Barça... el Athletic estaba enfadado con el Barça por sus formas. A partir de ahí, yo entablo conversaciones y llega un momento en la negociación, en la situación, en la que Nico no puede estar sin jugar. Nico es un Fórmula 1 y si yo voy a tu casa yo no me pudo comer tu problema y así se lo hice saber al Barça. A partir de ahí decidimos que si no había ciertas garantías, no podíamos arriesgarnos a que Nico no fuese allí para no jugar, habiendo un Mundial como había, y no ya habiendo un Mundial, es que es un profesional que tiene que ejercer su profesión. Yo voy a tu casa a ejercer mi profesión, tengo que seguir haciendo mi profesión, y si tú tienes un problema a mí eso no me tiene que afectar. Y si no me das seguridad de que no me va a afectar, entonces igual tengo que cambiar de opinión". ¿Con quién negociaba? "Con Deco, sí". Verano de 2024 y 2025: "Hubo contactos el verano de la Eurocopa muy importantes y el siguiente verano más importantes todavía. No es que hubiera cambios, la dinámica era buena, pero cuando llegas a un punto tú defiendes lo tuyo y yo, como os he dicho desde el minuto 0, lo que siempre voy a hacer es defender a mi jugador, siempre, a muerte. Y cuando tiene datos, lógica y sentido común lo que estás haciendo, nadie te puede decir nada. Yo pido algo que es esencial en la vida de un profesional, me da igual futbolista que camarero. Si eres camarero y no puedes ejercer tu profesión estás jodido. A partir de ahí las cosas cambian y se toma otro rumbo". ¿Enfrentamiento con el Barça? "Mientras vayas de frente y hagas las cosas bien, a mí nadie del Barça me puede decir nada. Hay que ir de cara y no engañar y no mentir. Lo harás mejor o peor, o estarás de acuerdo o no, pero eso no es que seas mala persona ni un cabrón, sino que haces bien tu trabajo". ¿Fue difícil la situación con el Athletic? "No fue difícil, el Athletic podía entender que Nico se iba a marchar. El Athletic entendía que Nico era un Fórmula 1 y que podía buscar otras alternativas. No hemos hablado de que renovó en diciembre de 2023 cuando en 2024 quedaba libre. Ahí renovamos tres años. Imaginaos Nico libre lo que podía tener, con la Eurocopa que hizo, que para mí fue el mejor jugador, aunque nos lo tangaron. Pero entendíamos que no podíamos irnos libres. Renovamos con la misma cláusula. Nos podíamos haber ido gratis con una prima de fichaje increíble y no lo hicimos. El chaval fue fiel al Athletic". ¿Nico quería salir? "Nico tenía idea de poder salir. Es ambicioso, en el Athletic sabes las limitaciones, sabes que no vas a ganar una Champions, posiblemente una Liga. Al final cuando él decía aquí no, aquí no, aquí no, aquí puede ser, pero la situación y lo que conlleva no cuadra, hay otra vuelta de tuerca que dices "¿y si renuevo?". Yo se lo planteo, le digo "Esto es lo que hay, ¿quieres que lo pelee?" Y él está de acuerdo. Y ahí renovamos".

articles.standfirst: Los de Giráldez siguen sin puntuar en Europa
articles.summary: Los de Giráldez siguen sin puntuar en Europa
articles.body: Veintiséis años después la Juventus se vengó del histórico 4-0 que sufrió en manos de aquel Celta que lideraba Alexander Mostovoi, llevándose la victoria en tiempo de descuento. Ninguno de los dos equipos es el mismo, ni el partido tenía la misma trascendencia del de hace un cuarto de siglo pero los de Claudio Giráldez volvieron a dejar escapar tres puntos de Balaídos. El Celta empieza a necesitar sumar en Europa. La inesperada derrota en Chipre, unida a la de este jueves, les deja con cero puntos en la clasificación y la próxima semana visitan al Celtic. Fue el primer gol para el canterano en la presente temporada, después de haber dado dos asistencias en Liga. También fue su primer gol en Europa League, en el que era su noveno encuentro. Un tanto que a la postre de nada sirvió. Claudio Giráldez presentó lo más parecido a su once de gala, teniendo en cuenta las bajas, y en el que no formó Iago Aspas, que participó en el último cuarto de partido, retornando a los terrenos de juego después de un mes lesionado. Hubo tres permutas, con respecto al partido de Elche, entrando en el once, Javi Rodríguez, Javi Rueda y Williot Swedberg.

articles.body:
A remarkable statistic, highlighting the impressive goalscoring rate of Real Madrid star Carlos Espí across the season to date has come to the fore online.

This of course comes fresh off the young frontman finding the net for the latest occasion on Wednesday evening.

With Real Madrid desperately searching for a way back into things late in a Champions League meeting with AS Roma, the summer arrival in Spain's capital was introduced off the bench.

And en route to a rousing late comeback for Los Blancos, Espí set things in motion, netting within minutes of stepping foot on the pitch.

This marked the 21-year-old's third goal for Real Madrid since his summer arrival from Levante. Whilst this may not look like an overly impressive scoring rate, it should be noted that it has come in just 38 minutes of playing time.

Espí, all told, is therefore averaging a goal every 12-13 minutes on the pitch this season.

articles.title: Woltemade: ‘My best game for Juventus, I enjoy playing with Kolo Muani’
articles.summary: Nick Woltemade feels the 2-1 win over Celta Vigo was his ‘best game for Juventus’ and confirms he enjoys partnering Randal Kolo Muani, but won’t push Luciano...
articles.body:
Nick Woltemade feels the 2-1 win over Celta Vigo was his 'best game for Juventus' and confirms he enjoys partnering Randal Kolo Muani, but won't push Luciano Spalletti into changing.

The striker has scored in both his Europa League games now this season, after converting a penalty in the 5-0 victory over NEC.

VIGO, SPAIN – OCTOBER 15: Federico Gatti of Juventus controls the ball during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between Real Club Celta and Juventus at Estadio Balaidos on October 15, 2026 in Vigo, Spain. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images)

This was his first from open play in the Bianconeri jersey, pouncing on the poor Marcos Alonso chest down on a cross to use it as an accidental assist.

Kolo Muani then came off the bench to complete the turnaround in added time by nodding in the Andrea Cambiaso cross, after Hugo Alvarez had put Celta Vigo in front after just 18 minutes.

VIGO, SPAIN – OCTOBER 15: Nick Woltemade of Juventus breaks away from Ilaix Moriba of RC Celta de Vigo during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between Real Club Celta and Juventus at Estadio Balaidos on October 15, 2026 in Vigo, Spain. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images)

"I think this was my best game for Juve, obviously I can do better, but I am happy with the goal. A goal always helps confidence, fo course, that is important for a striker, and I want to keep getting stronger," Woltemade told Sky Sport Italia.

Much has been said about where the former Newcastle United striker ought to play, as Luciano Spalletti seems reticent to use him alongside Kolo Muani from the start, instead launching him off the bench.

"Of course I like playing with Kolo. When there is just one centre-forward, the defenders can focus on just marking one and it is easier for them, whereas with two of us we can divide up the space more."

VIGO, SPAIN – OCTOBER 15: Nick Woltemade of Juventus celebrates scoring his team's first goal with teammate Federico Gatti during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between Real Club Celta and Juventus at Estadio Balaidos on October 15, 2026 in Vigo, Spain. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images)

Kolo Muani said much the same thing, so if both strikers would prefer to play together, why don't they start like that at Juventus?

"I am not the coach, I trust my coach and think any choice he makes will be the right one. I am a good player, Kolo is a good player, so the decision is up to the coach, but as long as we keep scoring goals, everyone will be happy," replied a diplomatic Woltemade.

articles.title: Alabama has 'taken appropriate action' against fan who shoved Georgia linebacker in the helmet after Bulldogs' win
articles.summary: The school said it had identified the fan who yelled at Wilson as he pushed him away after Georgia's 20-17 win.
articles.body:
Alabama says that it has "taken appropriate action" against a fan who as was seen pushing Georgia's Raylen Wilson in the helmet after the Bulldogs' win over the Crimson Tide in Week 6.

In a video posted to social media after the game, an irate Alabama fan makes contact with Wilson's helmet with his right hand and says, "Let's go boy, let's go boy, get the f*** out of here," as Wilson walks away from the stands and back toward the end zone.

"Alabama has identified and taken appropriate action against the individual involved in videos circulating on social media following Saturday night's football game," the athletic department told Al.com. "We take matters of this nature seriously and will not tolerate this behavior."

Georgia won the game 20-17 to move to No. 1 in the AP Top 25 following Texas' loss to Oklahoma earlier in the day. The Bulldogs clinched the game after a personal foul penalty on Alabama just before the two-minute warning allowed them to kneel out the clock. Earlier in the fourth quarter, officials also appeared to miss a blatant pass interference penalty on Georgia in the end zone.

After the game, ESPN shared a video to its social media channels of Alabama fans throwing objects onto the field as Georgia players went into the visiting team tunnel.

The win was Georgia's second straight over Alabama after the Tide beat the Bulldogs in September of 2025. Georgia won the rematch between the teams in the SEC championship game to earn a first-round bye into the College Football Playoff. Both teams lost in the quarterfinals as Alabama fell to Indiana in the Rose Bowl and Georgia lost to Ole Miss in the Sugar Bowl.

articles.title: Benfica 4-1 Celtic: Camilo Duran on target after birth of his child but Marin O'Neill's Hoops outclassed in Lisbon
articles.summary: Benfica were 3-0 up at half-time thanks to poor Celtic defending and while Camilo Duran pulled one back, Marco Silva's side ultimately proved too good; Martin O'Neill's Hoops have lost both Europa League games so far this season
articles.body:
Defensive mistakes from Celtic helped Marco Silva's hosts race into a three-goal lead by the break, with Jhon Duran at the double and Alexander Bah on the scoresheet.

Camilo Duran - who had made his own way to Portugal after staying in Scotland for the birth of his child - pulled one back for Martin O'Neill's side and hit a post as Celtic tried to set up a grandstand finish.

But instead, Vangelis Pavlidis wrapped up the scoring and a comprehensive win for Benfica, which leaves Celtic with two defeats from their first two games in the league phase.

There may have been encouragement in some of their second-half attacking play but alarm bells were ringing at the back.

In Lisbon, the city which hosted Celtic's greatest moment in the 1976 European Cup final, the visitors handed Benfica a head start when Dane Murray kicked the back of Jhon Duran's leg in a crowded box. The former Aston Villa striker was cool with his panenka penalty.

Sebastian Tounekti then switched off for Bah to volley in before Auston Trusty and Celtic keeper Vijami Sinisalo contrived to let Jhon Duran score from what appeared an impossible position for the third.

Celtic were desperately unlucky not to bring the game back to 2-1 before that, with Kasper Hogh hitting a post from close range before Camilo Duran curled the rebound against both the crossbar and the other post. And it would not be the last time the frame of the goal was rattled.

Fredrik Aursnes nodded against a post at the other end, from what was eventually flagged an offside position, while Andreas Schjelderup and Tomas Araujo hit the woodwork in the second half, with Camilo Duran's strike against an upright in between. Fine margins in those moments - but the difference between these sides was far greater.

4: PENALTY TO BENFICA! Murray kicks Jhon Duran in the back of the leg as he goes to make a clearance in a crowded penalty area.

5: GOAL! DURAN WITH THE PANENKA! Cool as you like from the Colombian striker who dinks in the opener.

23: GOAL! It's cute from the impressive Gianluca Prestianni, who lifts a cross into the box for Bah to volley in - but it's terrible from Tounekti, who goes to sleep and allows Bah to run off him and into space to convert.

25: SIDE-NETTING! Jhon Duran fires the wrong side of the near post and Celtic are on the ropes here.

28: CELTIC SO UNLUCKY! Hogh volleys against the upright from Tounekti's cross before Camilo Duran bends a follow-up shot against the crossbar and post.

35: OFF THE POST! But the offside flag goes up. Jhon Duran meets a corner and heads it into the six-yard box but Fredrik Aursnes nodded against the post before being flagged offside.

36: GOAL! Trusty tries to show Jhon Duran away from goal but the striker hooks his foot around the ball and somehow angles an effort past Sinisalo at his near post.

63: GOAL! Camilo Duran pulls one back for the Hoops, heading in sub Haissem Hassan's cross.

72: OFF THE POST! Sub Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain feeds Camilo Duran in the box and he crashes a left-foot strike against the near upright!

74: OFF THE POST! Andreas Schjelderup now goes close for Benfica!

89: GOAL! Pavlidis runs in behind and clinically fires low into the net from the edge of the box to make it 4-1.

90: OFF THE FRAME AGAIN! Araujo heads Pavlidis' cross against the bar!

O'Neill retains qualification hope after 'terrific' second half

Celtic boss Martin O'Neill to TNT Sports:

"It's the last thing you want to do, concede so early on. At 2-0 we have a great chance to make it 2-1 and then in a few minutes they make it 3-0. We could have capitulated but I thought the second half performance was really terrific.

"We created chance after chance, we should have scored more goals, and of course you're going to leave yourself a bit open at the end. But this second-half performance gives me the determination. I think we can still qualify. I know it's down to six games. We can still do it.

"Overall, I'm really, really delighted with the second-half performance and it's a shame we conceded the three goals first of all."

McGregor: Second-half performance something to hang onto

Celtic captain Callum McGregor to TNT Sports:

"A disappointing result. We're here to try to get points and win but we played against a really good side, with really good quality in the final third. First half we didn't really help ourselves, in terms of the unforced errors that lead to the goal, but second half gives us a bit to hang onto in terms of performance. We scored one, could have scored another couple as well. A game of two halves."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Brighton 4-0 Kauno Zalgiris: Georginio Rutter scores twice as Seagulls thrash Lithuanian side in Conference League
articles.summary: Match report as Brighton thrash Kauno Zalgris to get off to flying start in Europa Conference League; Georginio Rutter scores two and gets an assist, with Jack Hinshelwood and Matt O’Riley also on target for Fabian Hurzeler’s side
articles.body:
Brighton were dominant from the first whistle to the last against the Lithuanian Cup winners and took the lead through Rutter, but only after a VAR check. The ball had initially been deemed to have gone out of play before Ibrahim Osman's cut-back to the Dutchman, but the goal was awarded after review.

Rutter then turned provider as Brighton doubled their lead on the stroke of half-time when Hinshelwood - returning to the side for the first time since the Premier League opening weekend - slotted into the corner.

The third came after a lung-bursting run from Malick Yalcouye, who played Osman through to cross for Rutter to turn into the net with ease.

Matt O'Riley made it four with a header as he scored his first Brighton goal since August 2025. The Australia international should have got his second with another header late on, but was denied by an excellent save from Tomas Svedkauskas.

It is now five straight wins in all competitions for Fabian Hurzeler's side who host rivals Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

articles.title: Bournemouth 3-0 Sturm Graz: Cherries win first ever home European game as they make it two from two in Europa League
articles.summary: Match report as Bournemouth win their first-ever home European game, beating Sturm Graz; Evanilson scored at the end of the first half to hand the Cherries the lead; Rayan and an Alvaro Rodriguez penalty added after the break; Bournemouth face AC Milain in the Europa League next Thursday
articles.body:
It makes it two wins from two for the competition debutants and perhaps more importantly, they held on to a lead they took towards the end of the first half - something they have been unable to do in a poor start to the Premier League.

Evanilson will go down as the man who scored the first European goal at the Vitality Stadium and it was a thing of beauty. Adam Smith - captaining a team he joined in England's third tier 16 years ago - found him with a cross, with the Brazilian curling a powerful header past the goalkeeper from 15 yards out.

Sturm Graz came out with intent at the start of the second half and could have equalised just after the hour. Jurgen Heil smashed the woodwork before Djorde Petrovic was needed to keep out Jacob Hodl's follow-up.

But the Cherries rode the wave and doubled their lead through another Brazilian, Rayan. It was a howler from Daniil Khudyakov, whose spilled save from a corner landed to the Bournemouth forward. His low, fizzing shot then sped through the goalkeeper's outstretched hands.

And in second-half added time, Bournemouth were awarded a penalty. Former Huddersfield man Jon Gorenc Stankovic was penalised for a foul on James Hill - also coming in the aftermath of a Bournemouth corner.

Summer signing Alvaro Rodriguez stepped up to chip the spot kick in for his first Bournemouth goal, sealing another three points. It puts the Cherries fifth in the Europa League league phase table ahead of welcoming Ruben Amorim's AC Milan to the Vitality next Thursday.

Key moments from the Vitality Stadium...

12: CHANCE! Smith curls in a wonderful cross for the incoming Tavernier, but he's defended well as his attempt goes wide.

29: NO GOAL! The ball is in the back of the net for Bournemouth - but it's immediately ruled out for a handball against Bafode Diakate.

33: OFF THE POST!! Tavernier's curling effort hits the woodwork.

41: PENALTY?! REFEREE SAYS NO! Sturm Graz have their best attack of the half, with calls for a penalty after Beganovic goes down. He is unfairly booked after, but looked to already be losing his footing as Smith made contact.

43: GOAL! Evanilson gives Bournemouth the lead with an incredible curling header from some distance.

63: OFF THE POST! SAVE! Heil hits the post with a thunderous effort from the right, before Hodl's follow-up is stopped by Djorde Petrovic's legs.

76: GOAL! Rayan's low, hard shot beats Khudyakov after some poor goalkeeping.

90+2: PENALTY SCORED! Stankovic fouls Hill as he strikes inside the box and Bournemouth are awarded a penalty. Rodriguez scores from the spot.

Bournemouth captain Adam Smith to TNT Sports : "It's been a long time coming. The fans were up for it, the players were up for it so we're very happy with the performance.

"It wasn't my best cross [for Evanilson's goal], but I put it into the area and what a finish from him. It's a great header. He's deserved it because he's worked very hard this season and many more to come from him.

"We deserved that bit of luck and from there, we went on to win the game. In the second half, we got a bit tired but the quality that came off the bench is great. We look forward to Sunday now."

On if this can be a springboard for Bournemouth: "It was very disappointing at the weekend [against Chelsea]. We let ourselves down as players, we know that. We had a chat with each other and got a reaction today.

"That's a Bournemouth performance right there, but the week is not done. We have a massive game against Sunderland and we need to get three points."

'This needs to be a springboard for Bournemouth's season'

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Mark McAdam at the Vitality: "Back-to-back wins in the Europa League!

"Not a classic by any stretch but one that will live long in the memories for Bournemouth fans; their first ever taste of European football at the Vitality - a real moment in history. A game they dominated across the pitch from start to finish.
